Any request with a valid date raises NameError → 500. The endpoint is non-functional.

The new production behaviour — the /api/day-log Flask handler — has no real test. issues.detail: Key mismatch: handle registered under run_key=(app.name, slot) (a tuple) while _Tee.write -> run_logger.write_line is keyed on _RUN_APP.get()==app.name (a str, set by process_ticket's set_run_app(app.name), cockpit_state.py:415 / loop.py:1332). _resolve_key (run_logger.py:99) returns the supplied run_key verbatim, so _log_handles has the tuple key but write_line looks up the string key -> no match -> nothing is ever written. The per-ticket file stays 0 bytes, which is worse than the prior 222-byte note and reintroduces the 'silently empty per-ticket file' write_note_log exists to prevent (run_logger.py:176).

New test cannot detect the defect: TEST 1/2 stub open_run_log/close_run_log to Recorders (never opening a real file), so they only prove the calls happen, not that content lands. There is no assertion that a per-ticket file is non-empty after a build. TEST 3's assertion `not any(kw.get('run_key',(None,))[0] == 'F-1' ...)` is vacuous — run_key is (app.name, slot) so [0] is always 'alpha', never a ticket id; the 'no close after a failed open' claim is not actually verified.

Design tension for the fix: even if the handle is registered under app.name to match _Tee, two disjoint-footprint tickets of the SAME app can co-schedule (the footprint-conflict guard permits it), both setting _RUN_APP='alpha' and both registering under 'alpha'. open_run_log's defensive _close_handle(key) (run_logger.py:129) would then close the first slot's handle when the second opens, interleaving/losing lines. This is the exact multi-run clobber the serial EU-253 path sidesteps with write_note_log, so true per-ticket isolation under a concurrent drain needs per-(app,slot) attribution in _Tee/_RUN_APP, not just a key swap.

issues.detail: Runlog reconnect race: the scheduled setTimeout(startRunlogStream,4000) does not check for an already-open runlogEs before assigning a new EventSource. If a board-driven ticket-change restart (2810-2819) lands within the 4s reconnect window, the previously-created EventSource is orphaned (never closed) and two 'log' listeners unshift into the same runlogBuffer, duplicating lines. Low probability and it mirrors the board stream's accepted pattern (2678), which the ticket explicitly told the builder to copy.

Header clock (#gentime) is refreshed only in the SSE 'board' listener (2676); the 5s poll fallback path (tick -> applyBoard, 2662) never updates it, so under fallback the clock freezes. Also new Date().toLocaleTimeString() may render a locale format (e.g. '2:30:45 PM') differing from the server's initial %H:%M:%S. Cosmetic; the dim streamdot already signals stale state.

Coverage is a static source-grep guard (repo convention for the inline warroom JS, which can't run in-process). It asserts the six patterns exist but cannot exercise runtime behaviour (focus-guard early return, reconnect dedup, scroll-keep). Acceptable given the repo has no JS test harness.

issues.detail: Ticket said to assume POST /api/dismiss-result already existed and add no server-side logic, but the endpoint did not exist so the builder added it (server.py). This is a justified, well-documented, in-scope addition — the handler is inert without it — and stays confined to the ticket's surface (no dep/lockfile/unrelated-app churn). Recorded for traceability only.

The JS removes btn.closest('div'), which relies on _result_strip being a single flat <div> (verified: it is). If the strip markup ever gains an inner wrapper <div>, closest('div') would remove only the inner node. A data-attribute-anchored selector (e.g. closest('[data-dismiss-result]').closest('.result-strip')) would be more robust, but not required today.
